changes.text: [rework] Management: Investment accounts became general-purpose Accounts
sub: An account can now hold any kind of transaction — earnings, expenses, or contributions — not just investments; a “Merchandising” account can track its own sales and costs the same way a brokerage account tracks contributions

Click an account to expand it in place and see its stats (Earned/Spent/Invested/Value), an optional goal with a progress bar, and its own transaction list, plus one-tap +Earning/+Expense/+Invest buttons
The separate “Investment accounts” and “Budgets” (period spending limit) sections are gone — just Accounts now; anything not assigned to an account lands in “Other transactions” instead
Section headers carry a “?” that explains what they're for on hover, using the same stylized tooltip the Beta/Experimental/Recommended tags use elsewhere instead of a plain browser tooltip
Existing budget-limit data isn't deleted, just no longer shown

changes.text: [rework] Oracle now draws from topics instead of pages
sub: Same mechanic — draws two things and asks what connects them — just topics now, using tags from whichever page a topic lives on for the shared/contrast prompts
New: Manage connections — lists every link Oracle (or you) has drawn between two topics, each removable, plus a way to add one directly between two topics without waiting for a draw to pair them
“Link them” records the connection on the topic now, not the page
Removed the old “jump to Oracle” shortcut on the Entries panel — it pointed at a pool Oracle hasn't drawn from in a while

changes.text: [new] An explicit way to create a topic
sub: “+ Topic” in the page toolbar prompts for a name and adds it as a heading at the end of the page, caret ready to write underneath
Headings still become topics automatically just by typing one — this is just a clearer, more discoverable alternative to needing to already know that

changes.text: [redesign] Notebook legend is a real cover page now, not a table of contents
sub: A notebook's own color, name, and page/topic counts up top, the way a book's title page introduces what follows
Each page is a card — a text preview, its tags, and its topics as pill buttons — instead of a numbered serif index
Shown whenever a notebook has no page open, or any time from the Legend button in the sidebar

changes.text: [new] The page tasks panel can switch to a Navigation view
sub: Click the panel's header (Tasks / Navigation) to open a small menu — Navigation lists every topic on the current page and jumps straight to it with a scroll and a highlight flash
Doesn't touch the cross-page “Back to…” trail the way following a topic link to another page does — it's a same-page shortcut
The collapsed strip's label now matches whichever view is actually active, instead of always reading “Tasks”
The switcher's title and toggle arrow are anchored to the left, next to each other, instead of the arrow drifting off to the right
This week / This month / This year — a headline hours total, a bar chart (days, weeks, or months depending on the period) that animates in, and how it compares to the period before
Quick stats: sessions logged, busiest day/week/month, and your current streak
Toggle it off from Preferences like any other Productivity section, same as Medals or Weekly history

changes: [redesign] Productivity is out of Beta; Management is now tagged Experimental instead of Beta

changes.text: [new] Lock a page against edits or deletion
sub: A Lock button sits in the page toolbar between Pin and Delete — locked pages can't be typed in, formatted, tagged, or deleted until unlocked again

Covers every way a page could still be edited around a simple read-only flag — toolbar formatting commands, keyboard shortcuts, paste, drag-and-drop, and the table right-click menu, not just typing directly into the text
Delete shows a reminder to unlock first instead of the usual confirmation

changes.text: [new] Sessions can be logged or moved to a specific project
sub: Logging time by hand now has a project picker (once there's more than one project), defaulting to whichever one you're in
The session edit modal can reassign a session to a different project after the fact
The Sessions list shows which project a session belongs to when you're not already filtered to one

changes.text: [redesign] Patch notes and the update-available screen are cleaner
sub: A version's changes used to render as a solid tinted box; several stacked (common if you're a few versions behind) read as a wall of identical cards — now just a version label and a thin rule, so multiple versions read as one continuous list
A downgrade warning still gets the heavier callout treatment, since that one should stand out
Both screens now open with a small mark next to the heading instead of a bare heading
A change's deeper sub-details now sit behind a collapsed “N details” toggle instead of always being shown

changes.text: [fix] A notebook's own timeline stopped showing up when opened from Notebooks
sub: A shared CSS class between the timeline pointer and an unrelated empty-state message meant the pointer was always hidden in both states — the rule meant to hide the empty-state caught the pointer too

changes.text: [fix] A plain to-do with no due date could show up on the calendar marked overdue
sub: A due-date-less task still keeps a real date internally as bookkeeping — it was never meant to land on the calendar at all, but the calendar's day-matching logic didn't know to skip it
Now excluded at the source, so it can't appear on the month grid, a day's plan list, or Home's mini calendar — only in the Tasks card's dedicated “No due date” group, where it always belonged

changes.text: [fix] Clear Formatting didn't always fully clear a quote imported from elsewhere
sub:
A quote made in-app is a flat
; one pasted in or converted from markdown commonly arrives wrapped in an extra

— Clear Formatting's browser-native command only ever reached the inner wrapper, leaving the quote styling stuck
Fixed at the one place all page content already flows through (paste, load, save, markdown conversion) so it self-heals regardless of where a quote came from
Also fixes pressing Enter after a pasted quote behaving like Shift+Enter — same root cause: the nested wrapper meant the browser only ever split the inner paragraph instead of starting a new quote

changes.text: [fix] Merge duplicates could combine sessions from different projects
sub: Auto-detected duplicate groups now require a matching project, not just a matching day and label
A merged session now keeps its project instead of losing it — previously dropped regardless of source
Manually merging hand-picked sessions across projects now asks which project the result should keep, same as a disagreeing label or note already did

changes: [fix] The Welcome page was out of date — it listed Entries as a room (it's linked from pages/timelines now), called Productivity “Work,” and never mentioned Management, page locking, or Topics
Added more modular support for developers
Added compareVersions to support upadting from in the app
You can now view your current version and patch notes in preferences
Fixed a bug that caused daily tasks to dump up to ~175+ rows into your task list
compareVersions is now capable of reading pre-release versions via -dev
